correctness.rationale: Global vertex-to-block phase quotient coordinates are a diffeomorphism and separate the exact potential; the local sine equations have exactly six nondegenerate critical points with verified energies and Hessian inertias. The resulting polynomial is exact for all r. Chirality continuity gives a lower bound E_*+1/2, attained by an explicit path changing one block at a time. Morse handle theory applies below the next critical level: there are exactly 2^r index-zero cells and 3r2^(r-1) index-one cells, and explicit paths force connectivity, yielding the claimed bouquet rank. Finite original-coordinate gradient/Hessian and path checks across 3108 configurations and 40690 samples corroborate critical calculations but are not used as a general proof. Unit coupling, phase quotient, connected graph, and open level intervals are explicit.

value.rationale: Frustrated Kuramoto cacti have exponentially many chiral competing minima; the exact height and topology of the lowest connecting energy barrier are natural invariants directly relevant to switching under perturbations. The all-r polynomial simultaneously enumerates energies and unstable dimensions, and the first critical-level wedge formula establishes nontrivial homotopy not implied by stable-count data. The shape-independent 1/2 barrier, topological merger of 2^r components, and symmetry-exact windmill basin split form a motivated, reproducible infinite-family classification beyond a local toy computation.
